1.why: All seven screens are static with a plain card layout and no animations, moving images, or pop-ups are visible.

2.why: Step headings, labeled inputs, and teal primary buttons stand out clearly, though the large dark Logs panel competes for attention on every screen.

3.why: Each screen presents a single task with one labeled field and one button, but the user must scroll to the Logs panel at the bottom to retrieve the token and code.

4.why: Password rules and the required token/code are displayed on screen so little must be memorized, though the long recovery token would be burdensome if typed manually.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, password manager prompt, or autofill affordance is visible on any screen; only plain input fields appear.

6.why: The token and confirmation code are shown in the Logs panel for recognition, but no saved-item or familiar-item recognition features are present.

7.why: Step instructions are short and plain (e.g., 'Use 12 or more characters...'), but the repeated 'Protect your account' notice is a dense paragraph and the log text is technical jargon.

8.why: No error messages appear in any of the seven screenshots, so whether they describe problems and fixes cannot be confirmed.

9.why: The Logs panel literally shows the exact token and code (e.g., 'confirmation code = 482916') to type, and the password format is described, though no example password is given.

10.why: No choices between authentication methods (password, code, face login) are offered; each step allows only a single fixed input method.

11.why: Every screen presents exactly one input field and one action button, so the user never faces multiple simultaneous choices.

12.why: Outcomes are stated via clear headings ('Sign-in confirmed', 'Privacy conditions accepted') and corresponding log entries like 'Recovery token verified in this secure session.'

13.why: Each new step includes a short instructional tip (e.g., 'You may paste or manually type the token'), but no dedicated help link or guidance feature exists.

14.why: No error state, retry button, or 'resend code' option is visible in any screenshot, so easy recovery from mistakes cannot be observed.

15.why: The header, card layout, button style, security notice, Logs panel, and footer are identical across all seven steps, providing full visual consistency.
